---
# PROMPT S1 — "Rebuild my Quarto + Shiny dashboard as a STATIC Quarto dashboard that runs
# entirely in the browser (Observable JS), so it can sit on a plain web host behind a
# password. Load small aggregated 'cubes' exported from the DuckDB warehouse, re-aggregate
# them client-side for every filter, and keep the same pages: overview, semantic layer,
# customer voice, marketing & macro, data quality. Link back to the master tutorial."
title: "TDBG Growth Cockpit"
author: "Static edition · runs in your browser"
format:
  dashboard:
    theme: [cosmo, theme.scss]
    orientation: rows
    nav-buttons:
      - icon: book
        href: ../book/index.html
        aria-label: Master tutorial
      - icon: journal-code
        href: ../notebook.html
        aria-label: Build notebook
      - icon: github
        href: https://github.com/adibongo/tdbg2/tree/main/platform/lab
        aria-label: Source code
resources:
  - data/*
---


# {.sidebar}

::: {style="display:none"}
```{ojs}
// PROMPT S2 — "Load the cubes once and write one aggregation function whose formulas mirror
// semantic/metrics.yml, so every number on the page uses the governed definitions."
cube   = FileAttachment("data/cube_week.csv").csv({typed: true})
prod   = FileAttachment("data/cube_product.csv").csv({typed: true})
layer  = FileAttachment("data/metrics.json").json()
tests  = FileAttachment("data/tests.json").json()
srcs   = FileAttachment("data/sources.json").json()
build  = FileAttachment("data/build.json").json()
recon  = FileAttachment("data/recon.csv").csv({typed: true})
mkt    = FileAttachment("data/marketing.csv").csv({typed: true})
macro  = FileAttachment("data/macro.csv").csv({typed: true})
gdp    = FileAttachment("data/gdp.csv").csv({typed: true})
reviews = FileAttachment("data/reviews.json").json()

NAVY = "#0B2C55"
GOLD = "#E8A33D"
PAL = ["#0B2C55", "#E8A33D", "#7FA8D4", "#6FBFAE", "#9B8EC4", "#A9C86B", "#F2C14E", "#E58B3C"]
wkStr = d => (d instanceof Date ? d.toISOString().slice(0, 10) : String(d))
monthsAll = [...new Set(cube.map(d => wkStr(d.wk).slice(0, 7)))].sort()
regionsAll = [...new Set(cube.map(d => d.region))].sort()
catsAll = [...new Set(cube.map(d => d.category))].sort()

agg = rows => {
  const s = {rev: 0, gp: 0, units: 0, n: 0, so: 0, disc: 0, rev_promo: 0, n_promo: 0}
  for (const r of rows) { s.rev += r.rev; s.gp += r.gp; s.units += r.units; s.n += r.n; s.so += r.so;
    if (r.promo === 1) { s.rev_promo += r.rev; s.n_promo += r.n; s.disc += (r.disc || 0) } }
  return s
}
METRIC = {
  // JS mirrors of the SQL in metrics.yml: same names, and sum first, divide last
  const m = {}
  m.revenue = s => s.rev
  m.units = s => s.units
  m.gross_profit = s => s.gp
  m.gross_margin_pct = s => 100 * s.gp / s.rev
  m.avg_selling_price = s => s.rev / s.units
  m.stockout_rate_pct = s => 100 * s.so / s.n
  m.promo_share_pct = s => 100 * s.rev_promo / s.rev
  m.avg_discount_pct = s => s.n_promo ? 100 * s.disc / s.n_promo : NaN
  return m
}
fmt = (v, f) => !isFinite(v) ? "—" : f === "naira" ? (Math.abs(v) >= 1e9 ? `₦${(v/1e9).toFixed(2)}bn` : Math.abs(v) >= 1e6 ? `₦${(v/1e6).toFixed(1)}m` : `₦${Math.round(v).toLocaleString()}`)
  : f === "pct" ? `${v.toFixed(1)}%` : Math.round(v).toLocaleString()
```
:::

::: {style="display:none"}
```{ojs}
// Derived data (hidden): filters applied once, reused by every card
keep = r => { const m = wkStr(r.wk !== undefined ? r.wk : r.mon).slice(0, 7);
  return m >= m0 && m <= m1 && regions.includes(r.region) && cats.includes(r.category) &&
         (promo === "All" || (promo === "On promo" ? r.promo === 1 : r.promo === 0)) }
fcube = cube.filter(keep)
fprod = prod.filter(keep)
fm = mkt.filter(d => { const m = wkStr(d.wk).slice(0, 7); return m >= m0 && m <= m1 })
ch = d3.rollups(fm, v => ({spend: d3.sum(v, d => d.spend_ngn) / 1e6, conv: d3.sum(v, d => d.conversions)}), d => d.channel)
  .map(([channel, s]) => ({channel, ...s, cpa: s.spend * 1e6 / s.conv}))
mac = macro.filter(d => { const m = wkStr(d.mon).slice(0, 7); return m >= m0 && m <= m1 })
  .flatMap(d => [["Headline CPI", d.headline], ["Food CPI", d.food], ["MPR", d.mpr]].map(([s, v]) => ({m: new Date(d.mon), s, v})))
openm = FileAttachment("data/open_macro.csv").csv({typed: true})
thisYear = new Date().getFullYear()
imfN = openm.filter(d => d.source === "IMF" && d.iso3 === "NGA" && ["PCPIPCH", "NGDP_RPCH"].includes(d.indicator) && d.year >= 2015)
wdiInds = [...new Map(openm.filter(d => d.source === "World Bank").map(d => [d.indicator, d.indicator_name])).entries()]
```
:::

```{ojs}
// PROMPT S3 — "Sidebar filters that every page respects: month range, regions, categories, promotion."
viewof m0 = Inputs.select(monthsAll, {label: "From", value: monthsAll[0]})
viewof m1 = Inputs.select(monthsAll, {label: "To", value: monthsAll[monthsAll.length - 1]})
viewof regions = Inputs.checkbox(regionsAll, {label: "Region", value: regionsAll})
viewof cats = Inputs.checkbox(catsAll, {label: "Category", value: catsAll})
viewof promo = Inputs.radio(["All", "On promo", "Full price"], {label: "Promotion", value: "All"})
```

  <b>${fcube.length.toLocaleString()}</b> cube rows in view.<br>
  Warehouse built ${build.length ? String(build[0].built_at).slice(0,16) : ""} · ${build.length ? build[0].fact_rows.toLocaleString() : ""} fact rows.<br>
  Static edition: filters run in your browser. The live Shiny edition can also switch between data sources: see the <a href="../index.html">platform page</a>.</div>`

card = (m, bg, fg) => html`<div title="${layer.metrics[m].description}" style="background:${bg};color:${fg};border-radius:8px;padding:12px 14px;height:100%">
  <div style="font-size:.78rem;opacity:.85">${layer.metrics[m].label}</div>
  <div style="font-family:'Source Serif 4',Georgia,serif;font-size:1.65rem;font-weight:700">${fmt(METRIC[m](kp), layer.metrics[m].format)}</div></div>`

  ${card("revenue", NAVY, "#fff")}${card("gross_margin_pct", "#F7F4ED", NAVY)}${card("units", "#F7F4ED", NAVY)}
  ${card("stockout_rate_pct", "#FCEBD7", "#8A4B0F")}${card("promo_share_pct", GOLD, NAVY)}</div>`

## Row {height=18%}

```{ojs}
// PROMPT S5 — "Let users pick any governed metric, a dimension and a time grain; show the SQL the
// live app would compile from metrics.yml next to the chart computed in the browser."
metricKeys = Object.keys(METRIC)
viewof met = Inputs.select(metricKeys, {label: "Metric", value: "revenue", format: k => layer.metrics[k].label})
viewof dim = Inputs.select(["region", "category", "depot", "promo", "(none)"], {label: "Break down by", value: "category"})
viewof grain = Inputs.select(["quarter", "month", "week", "year", "(none)"], {label: "Time grain", value: "quarter"})
```

## Row {height=82%}

```{ojs}
//| title: The SQL the live app compiles from metrics.yml
period = (w, g) => { const s = wkStr(w); const y = s.slice(0, 4), m = +s.slice(5, 7);
  return g === "week" ? s : g === "month" ? s.slice(0, 7) : g === "quarter" ? `${y}-Q${Math.ceil(m / 3)}` : g === "year" ? y : "all" }
sqlText = {
  const sel = []; const grp = [];
  if (grain !== "(none)") { sel.push(`date_trunc('${grain}', week_starting) AS period`); grp.push("period") }
  if (dim !== "(none)") { const col = dim === "depot" ? "depot_name" : dim === "promo" ? "on_promotion" : dim; sel.push(`${col} AS ${dim}`); grp.push(dim) }
  sel.push(`${layer.metrics[met].sql} AS ${met}`)
  return `SELECT\n  ${sel.join(",\n  ")}\nFROM ${layer.table}` + (grp.length ? `\nGROUP BY ${grp.join(", ")}\nORDER BY ${grp[0]}` : "")
}
html`<pre style="background:#0B2C55;color:#F7F4ED;padding:12px;border-radius:6px;font-size:.8rem;white-space:pre-wrap">${sqlText}</pre>
<p style="font-size:.85rem"><b>${layer.metrics[met].label}:</b> ${layer.metrics[met].description}<br><i>Owner: ${layer.owner}</i></p>`
```

```{ojs}
//| title: Result
semRows = d3.rollups(fcube, v => METRIC[met](agg(v)), d => period(d.wk, grain), d => dim === "(none)" ? "All" : String(d[dim]))
  .flatMap(([p, gs]) => gs.map(([g, v]) => ({period: p, group: g, value: v}))).sort((a, b) => d3.ascending(a.period, b.period))
grain === "(none)"
  ? Plot.plot({width: 620, height: 380, marginLeft: 110, x: {label: layer.metrics[met].label, grid: true}, y: {label: null},
      marks: [Plot.barX(semRows, {y: "group", x: "value", fill: NAVY, sort: {y: "-x"}, tip: true})]})
  : Plot.plot({width: 620, height: 380, marginLeft: 60, color: {legend: true, range: PAL}, y: {label: layer.metrics[met].label, grid: true}, x: {label: null, tickRotate: -30},
      marks: [Plot.lineY(semRows, {x: "period", y: "value", stroke: "group", strokeWidth: 2, tip: true}), Plot.dot(semRows, {x: "period", y: "value", fill: "group", r: 2.5})]})
```

# Customer voice

## Row {height=14%}

```{ojs}
// PROMPT S6 — "Semantic search over the 4,938 reviews with the same TF-IDF + cosine method as the
// warehouse, computed in the browser."
viewof q = Inputs.text({label: "Search reviews", value: "debited twice no reversal", width: "100%", submit: "Search"})
```

## Row {height=86%}

```{ojs}
//| title: Closest reviews
index = {
  const tok = s => s.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9 ]/g, " ").split(/\s+/).filter(w => w.length > 2)
  const docs = reviews.map(r => tok(r.txt)); const df = new Map()
  for (const d of docs) for (const w of new Set(d)) df.set(w, (df.get(w) || 0) + 1)
  const idf = w => Math.log(reviews.length / (df.get(w) || reviews.length)) + 1
  const vec = d => { const v = new Map(); for (const w of d) if (df.has(w)) v.set(w, (v.get(w) || 0) + idf(w));
    const n = Math.hypot(...v.values()); for (const [k, x] of v) v.set(k, x / (n || 1)); return v }
  return {tok, vec, vecs: docs.map(vec)}
}
hits = {
  const qv = index.vec(index.tok(q))
  return reviews.map((r, i) => { let s = 0; for (const [k, x] of qv) s += x * (index.vecs[i].get(k) || 0); return {similarity: +s.toFixed(3), ...r} })
    .filter(d => d.similarity > 0).sort((a, b) => b.similarity - a.similarity).slice(0, 25)
}
hits.length ? Inputs.table(hits, {columns: ["similarity", "txt", "theme", "sentiment", "channel", "stars", "lang"],
  header: {txt: "review", lang: "language"}, width: {txt: 380}, rows: 14})
  : html`<p>None of those words appear in the reviews. TF-IDF matches words, not meaning; Chapter 11 of the tutorial shows the neural upgrade.</p>`
```

  x: {label: "reviews", grid: true}, y: {label: null},
  marks: [Plot.barX(reviews, Plot.groupY({x: "count"}, {y: "theme", fill: "sentiment", sort: {y: "-x"}, tip: true}))]})

//| title: Data tests (the publish gate)
chip = s => html`<span style="display:inline-block;padding:1px 8px;border-radius:10px;color:#fff;font-weight:700;font-size:.75rem;background:${s === "PASS" ? "#6FBFAE" : s === "WARN" ? GOLD : "#C2410C"}">${s}</span>`

${tests.map(t => { const s = t.status === "FAIL" && t.severity === "warn" ? "WARN" : t.status; return html`<tr><td>${chip(s)}</td><td>${t.test}</td><td>${t.detail}</td></tr>` })}
</tbody></table><p style="font-size:.8rem;color:#475569">FAIL blocks publishing. WARN reports only. Freshness warns because the course data ends in March 2026.</p>`
